title: Independent agent contexts — each agent keeps its OWN message history; the two debaters never share a conversation thread (separate per-agent context objects, anti-sycophancy §2) (Epic 5)
prompt:
Ensure each agent keeps its own message history. The two debaters must NOT share a conversation thread (anti-sycophancy). Wire separate context objects per agent.

Follow repo standards: TDD (write the failing test first, then code); max 150 lines per code file (split, don't compress); ruff = 0 violations + mypy clean; no hard-coded values (read from config); every external API call goes through the API gatekeeper (Epic 13); log via the LOG package; keep coverage >= 85%. Read docs/PRD.md and the relevant docs/prds/*.md before starting.
note: Plumbing for independent per-agent conversation contexts (PRD §5.4 / anti-sycophancy §2: 'Debaters never share a chat thread'). New module packages/core/src/agent_debate/core/agents/context.py. CONTEXT REPRESENTATION: a lightweight, typed, frozen Turn dataclass (role: Literal['user','assistant'] + content: str) per message — chosen over raw pydantic-ai ModelMessage so the container is trivially isolatable/JSON-friendly and easy for 5.5/5.6 to extend; Turn.to_model_message() maps it to pydantic-ai message_history (user -> ModelRequest[UserPromptPart], assistant -> ModelResponse[TextPart]) so the engine (Epic 6) can feed AgentContext.message_history() to agent.run(message_history=...). AgentContext holds an identity ('pro'/'con'/'controller') + a PRIVATE list of Turns with append_user/append_assistant; history() returns an immutable tuple snapshot (a copy). DebateContexts holder owns three DISTINCT AgentContext objects (pro/con/controller) exposed by role, with for_side(DebateSide)->pro|con; create_debate_contexts() builds three isolated empty contexts and logs via LOG (get_logger('agents') -> debate_contexts_created). Named constants: CONTROLLER_IDENTITY, Role type alias — no hard-coded role strings at call sites. ISOLATION (no shared thread, the core anti-sycophancy property) is PROVEN by tests: appending to the Pro context leaves the Con context empty (and vice versa), pro/con/controller are distinct objects (is-not), and each preserves its own ordered history. Re-exported AgentContext/DebateContexts/Turn/create_debate_contexts from agent_debate.core AND the full surface (+ Role + CONTROLLER_IDENTITY) from agent_debate.core.agents. 5.5 (side anchoring) and 5.6 (adversarial relay framing) seams left clean: append_user accepts an already-framed opponent message as a USER turn in the agent's OWN thread — never by sharing the opponent's raw history; the relay framing itself is NOT implemented here (that is 5.6). API gatekeeper (Epic 13): N/A — builds containers offline, no agent and no external/network call. TDD red-first: wrote packages/core/tests/test_agent_context.py first, watched it fail (ImportError: cannot import name 'AgentContext'), then implemented to green (15 tests). 150-line guideline: adding the 5.4 re-exports would have pushed core/__init__.py to 153 code lines, so per 'split, don't compress' the secondary names (Role, CONTROLLER_IDENTITY) are exported only from agent_debate.core.agents while the KEY context surface stays on agent_debate.core, keeping the hub at 149 code lines and __all__ an explicit literal (mypy/ruff re-export contract intact). Gates green locally: ruff=0, ruff format clean, mypy clean (109 files), pytest 436 passed, context.py + total coverage 100%, line-limit pass, secret-scan pass. See PR CI for authoritative result.
